brief: Creating a presentable presentation based on the Ubuntu CLI Cheat Sheet, covering system information, commands, system monitoring, file management, package management, and user management.

spec.title: Ubuntu CLI Cheat Sheet
spec.subtitle: Essential Operations and System Management
spec.author: System Administration Team

slides.title: Ubuntu Command Line Interface
slides.subtitle: A concise guide to system management, monitoring, and operations
slides.notes: This presentation serves as an executive quick-reference guide for standard Ubuntu CLI operations.

slides.title: System Information
bullets: uname -a: View all kernel and system information
hostnamectl: Display hostname and system architecture details
lscpu: Audit CPU architecture and core specifications
timedatectl status: Verify current system time and synchronization
slides.notes: Establish a baseline by querying the core system environment immediately upon login.

slides.title: Monitoring System Health

left.title: Process Overview
bullets: top: Real-time dynamic process monitoring
htop: Interactive, user-friendly process visualization

right.title: Resource Usage
bullets: df -h: Readable disk storage statistics
free -m: Current RAM utilization in megabytes

slides.notes: Prioritize htop for troubleshooting as it offers superior visualization over standard top.

slides.title: Executing Background Commands
slides.notes: Efficient process control minimizes terminal clutter during long-running tasks.

slides.title: Service Management
bullets: sudo systemctl start <service>: Initialize a specific service
sudo systemctl stop <service>: Halt an active service
sudo systemctl status <service>: Review current operational state
slides.notes: Systemd is the standard for service control; ensure sudo privileges are active.

slides.title: Core File & User Management

left.title: File Operations
bullets: ls: Directory contents listing
cp: Copy source to destination
mv: Move or rename files

right.title: User Administration
bullets: w: List currently logged-in sessions
sudo adduser: Create new system users

slides.notes: Standard file manipulation and user audit basics.

slides.title: Package & Network Management
bullets: sudo apt install <package>: Install software dependencies
apt search <package>: Locate specific repository packages
ip addr show: Inspect network interfaces and IP addresses
ping <host>: Verify network connectivity
slides.notes: Use apt for dependency resolution; always verify network interfaces before troubleshooting connectivity.

slides.title: Security & Firewall
bullets: sudo ufw status: Check active firewall rules
sudo ufw enable: Activate Uncomplicated Firewall
sudo pro attach <token>: Register system with Ubuntu Pro
sudo pro enable livepatch: Apply kernel security without reboots
slides.notes: Livepatch significantly reduces maintenance downtime by eliminating reboot cycles for patches.

slides.title: Operational Best Practices
slides.body: Maintain system integrity by utilizing package managers for software, enabling firewall protections by default, and streamlining kernel updates via Ubuntu Pro.
slides.notes: Summarize the philosophy of secure and stable Ubuntu administration.

slides.title: Next Steps
bullets: Audit existing servers for Ubuntu Pro compliance
Standardize monitoring tools across all environments
Review shell history for repetitive task automation
slides.notes: Encourage the team to integrate these commands into their daily workflow and automation scripts.

spec.notesForUser: No placeholder statistics used. All commands provided are based on the user's source material. Ensure your team has sudo access to perform systemctl, ufw, and pro commands.
